question: After 1500 cycles, what capacity does the cathode deliver per gram of sulfur and per gram of the whole electrode, and what sulfur share of the electrode does their ratio imply, against the sulfur content the paper states?
rendered: According to the paper, after 1500 cycles, the cathode delivers 306 mAh/gS (per gram of sulfur) and 87 mAh/g (per gram of the whole electrode). The ratio of these two capacities is 306 mAh/gS / 87 mAh/g = 3.52. The paper states that the sulfur content is 35 wt%. Therefore, the sulfur share of the electrode is 35 wt% / 100 wt% = 0.35, which is equivalent to 35 g/g. The ratio of the capacities implies that the cathode delivers 3.52 times more capacity per gram of sulfur than per gram of the whole electrode.
